AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The aim of this study was to review retrospectivelythe clinical presentations, indications for surgery and surgical outcomes of adolescent and adult patients who were diagnosed with colonic basidiobolomycosis in the last 10years.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The study was carried out in Aseer Central Hospital, Abha, Saudi Arabia by reviewing the medical files of all patients in the last 10 yearswho were diagnosed with colonic basidiobolomycosis and required surgical intervention.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were twenty two patients. Common findings in all patients were weight loss, abdominal pain, and an abdominal mass. The right colon was affected in 21 patients. The initial diagnosis was correct in 7 patients while 9 were thought to be malignant. All patients underwent colonic resection followed byat least one year of antifungal medical treatment. Intraoperatively, all patients had moderate or dense adhesions, an abdominal mass and lymphadenopathy. Most surgeons'had the impression intraoperatively that the diagnosis was inflammatory rather than malignant. Postoperatively, 3 patients died within 6 months of the operation due to progression of the disease. Four patients developed severe wound infections, 3 of whom had abdominal dehiscence and required re-closure.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Colonic basidiobolomycosis is alife-threatening fungal infection that should be considered a surgical condition. A high index of suspicion including basidiobolomycosis in the differential diagnosis for the acute abdomen with a colonic mass is required for a proper diagnosis. Early aggressive surgical management followed bya prolonged course of itraconazolepostoperatively could improve the outcome of the condition. This article is protected by copyright.
